locator.text: Equation (5.39), p. 59, in the proof of Lemma 5.4

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. No declaration was found stating this inequality: I found nothing bounding ‖D^m(F(U) − F(U^{[J]}))‖ by q^{-H_m}|e|_{m+s}(1+|U^{[J]}|_{m+s}+|e|_{m+s})^{d-1}, and no Lean object in this part of the development carries the paper's degree parameter d at all (Expression, GenericDifferentialPolynomial.lean:185-190, is an untyped syntax tree with no degree field). The Lean reaches the same place by another route: the differential polynomial is a syntax tree, and the comparison of F(U) with F(U^{[J]}) is propagated through it by structural induction (Expression.approximation_eval, line 217). At each product node ApproximationRates.mul performs the paper's own 'subtracting two monomials one factor at a time', splitting f·g − fs·gs = (f−fs)·g + fs·(g−gs) (lines 128 and 131) and adding the exponents: tailLoss m = max (maxJetLoss a.tailLoss m + maxJetLoss b.growthLoss m) (maxJetLoss b.tailLoss m + maxJetLoss a.growthLoss m). So the paper's factor (1 + |U^{[J]}|_{m+s} + |e|_{m+s})^{d-1} becomes an additive accumulation of the stage growth exponents over the remaining factors, the order shift m → m+s becomes ApproximationRates.directional bumping the jet index by one at each derivative node (line 162-164), and q^{-H_m} becomes a loss function of m alone, independent of J. The statement the paper derives from (5.39) and then uses — the difference has a J-independent loss, JetRate (f − stage J) m (gain J − loss m) — is what TailRates.rate records and what the rest of the Lean proof consumes; (5.39) itself, as a norm inequality in |e|_{m+s} and |U^{[J]}|_{m+s}, is not stated anywhere I found.
